resources.string: Helps you avoid getting pulled into Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts. When it detects you entering, it closes that section so you can keep doing what you were doing. Nothing leaves the device.
Without this, Basta! can\'t detect Reels. Tap it and enable Basta! in the list.
Without this, the system may kill the service after a few hours.
On your phone (%1$s), besides the battery exemption go to Settings → Apps → Basta! → Autostart and enable it. Otherwise the system will close the service in the background.

95 min/day. That\'s what we lose on average to Reels and Shorts. Almost an hour and a half. Every day.\n\nWhen you enter, this app pulls you out. No motivational coaches, no sermons.

string-array.name: tips_stats
string-array.item: The average user spends 95 min a day on Reels and Shorts. Almost a movie.
Your brain takes 23 min to recover focus after each distraction.
Reels plays 30 videos in 5 min. 30 micro-doses of dopamine.
Infinite scroll is designed so your brain never decides to stop.
1 hour of screen before bed = 22 min less deep sleep.
70% of users lose track of time on Reels.
TikTok hooks you in 8 min of use. Faster than coffee.
An average Reels session lasts 24 min. Almost half an episode of something good.
The younger the user, the more time on short video. You barely see it in grandparents.
Every like you get on Reels isn\'t yours. It\'s the algorithm deciding for you.
Teens with +3h/day on short video show 2x more anxiety symptoms.
60% of people check their phone in the first 10 min after waking up.
We spend on average 3h 15min a day on our phones. That\'s 49 full days a year.
Blue screen light delays melatonin release by 1.5 hours.

string-array.name: tips_alternatives
string-array.item: 5 min of Reels = 5 min reading. When did you last finish a whole book?
If you have 20 min, go for a walk. You can\'t see the sun while doomscrolling.
Call a friend. One conversation beats 100 reels combined.
Boredom is the signal that your brain is about to create something. Don\'t shut it off.
Cook something simple instead of scrolling. You eat better and you actually get what you wanted.
10 min of stretching when you wake up > 10 min of Reels in bed.
Write down 3 things you want to do today. Start with one, no thinking.
Step out on the balcony for 2 min. The screen isn\'t going anywhere.
20 squats right now give you more energy than 20 reels.
Writing a long message to someone you care about hits harder than any scroll.
A coffee with someone in person is worth a week of stories.
If you\'re bored, look out the window for 30 seconds. Seriously.
Listen to a song with your eyes closed. Enough as a break.
Put on a song and dance for 3 minutes. Your body will thank you.
Cold shower for 30 seconds. Better reset than 50 reels.
Water a plant. Brings the brain to something slow and alive.

string-array.name: tips_reflections
string-array.item: The first scroll isn\'t the problem. Number 50 is.
You don\'t have to be productive all the time. Being a little bored is fine too.
The hard part isn\'t quitting Reels. It\'s not opening them without thinking.
The algorithm remembers you every second. How much do you remember the algorithm?
Every time this app pulls you out, you gain time you didn\'t see slipping away.
Your free time isn\'t \"dead time.\" It\'s one of the few moments that are really yours.
Choose your distractions on purpose. The ones that catch you off guard hurt the most.
If you open Reels to \"rest,\" you end up more tired. Confirmed.
Real curiosity lasts hours. Reels curiosity, 8 seconds.
Close your eyes for 10 seconds. That\'s more rest than half an hour of scrolling.
Good things take time. Reels things arrive in 15 seconds and leave just as fast.
Attention is the scarcest resource of the century. And you give it away for free.
Question: whose was the last reel you watched? Exactly.
Before grabbing your phone, breathe three times. Sometimes the urge passes.
